anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text: Recommendation: drop the proposal, because the problem it solves does not exist. It adds a second way to read settings next to the existing resolver, the small helper that opens settings.json and picks the value each time the app asks for a setting. The proposal assumes settings are read only once at startup, so edits made during a session would go unnoticed. That assumption is wrong. The resolver re-reads settings.json on every call, so switching the display setting from compact to expanded already takes effect on the very next call, with no restart. Because the proposal runs both readers on every lookup, each request would read the settings file twice and still return the same updated value, adding work without changing what users see. It also does not fit how the project handles settings, since there would be two readers doing one job, and only one caller would use the new helper. Your decision is whether to add the second path or keep the existing resolver. My pick is to keep the existing resolver, because it already picks up edits immediately with half the file reads.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text: Keep the existing settings resolver, the helper that reads the settings file and picks the value for each call. The proposal adds a second reader to notice edits during a session, but its startup-only assumption is wrong: changing the display setting from compact to expanded already takes effect on the next call without restarting, so the new path would make two file reads instead of one for the same result and serve only one caller. The decision is whether to add the second path or keep the existing resolver; my pick is to keep the resolver because it already delivers the proposed benefit without the extra read or duplicate path.
